svg.text: Route 53 PHZ Delegation — DNS Resolution Sequence
dig app.dev.system.example.com: the numbered order Resolver actually evaluates the parent → child delegation chain (not the static topology — see overview.drawio.svg for that)
Primary sequence — dig app.dev.system.example.com from HubTestInstance (HubVpc)
VPC resolver finds NS+glue for dev.system.example.com inside the system.example.com zone
ParentDelegateRule (DelegationRecord=system.example.com) matches → hands off via Outbound endpoint to glue IPs 10.1.0.10 / 10.1.0.42
query reaches DevVpc's Inbound Delegation endpoint via Transit Gateway
DevVpc resolver answers from its own dev.system.example.com zone: app.dev.system.example.com → A 10.1.200.10
answer returns the same path: Dev Inbound Delegation EP → TGW → Hub Outbound EP → HubVpc Resolver → HubTestInstance, which prints 10.1.200.10
Secondary sequence — same query, originating from on-premises BIND9 (OnPremVpc)
BIND9 (OnPremVpc) → HubVpc's regular Inbound endpoint (not Outbound) — its only configured forward zone is system.example.com

rejoins the primary flow at step 2: same NS+glue lookup, same ParentDelegateRule, same Transit Gateway hop, same 10.1.200.10 answer — BIND9 never needed to know dev.system.example.com or stg.system.example.com
